T.title: Fact or Rumor?
T.intro: The Planning Board meets next week. People in town are saying lots of things. Some are checked facts. Some are rumors. Some, nobody knows yet.
T.how: Tap 'Peek at the source' to see who said it and how they know. Then tap the box where it goes.

ok.fact: Yes! We checked what the dated proposal says. A proposal is not a promise that it will happen.
ok.rumor: Yes! Nobody can show how they know. Rumors come from hopeful and worried people.
ok.dontknow: Yes! It isn't studied or decided yet. 'We don't know yet' is an honest answer.

T.chat: A message in the family chat
T.can: I can check who said it and how they know.

$parts: Next time, peek first, even when

T.tipPeek: Next time, tap 'Peek at the source' before you sort.
T.tipRumor: Next time, if nobody can show how they know, choose Rumor.
T.tipDk: Next time, look for a study or a decision that isn't done yet.
T.tipFact: Next time, check what the source actually proves. A dated proposal tells us what is proposed, not what will happen.
T.tip100: Great checking! Try a new round with new claims.
T.real: Next time you hear 'Everyone says…', ask a grown-up: 'Who said it? How do they know?'
T.guText: Kids check a claim's source before sorting it as a checked fact, a rumor or 'we don't know yet'. Rumors in the game come from both sides, for example 'the lights will go out' and 'it uses no water at all'. Health effects for a site that isn't built yet go under 'we don't know yet'.
T.sourceFiction: This document is made up for Pecan Grove. It is not a real company plan.
planExcerpt: Water: This plan expects daily water use. A water-use estimate is part of the proposal.
Jobs: The plan lists many jobs while building and fewer jobs after opening.
Backup engines: The plan says they would run during power cuts and short tests.
This is a proposal, not an approval or a promise about future results.

bank.b0001: It's written in the plan the company sent to Regional Review. Anyone can read it at the library.
bank.b0003: The State Environment Office is still checking the air permit.
bank.b0005: The sound study isn't done yet.
bank.b0007: The Development Board hasn't decided about tax breaks yet.
bank.b0009: A friend of a friend told them.
bank.b0010: They heard it at a ball game. Nobody checked.
bank.b0011: Lots of people passed it on. Nobody knows who said it first.
bank.b0012: Someone saw it online and can't find it again.
bank.b0014: It uses no water at all.
bank.b0015: Every well in town will dry up next year.
bank.b0016: The company's September 3 proposal lists a daily water-use estimate.
bank.b0017: Everyone in Pecan Grove will get a job there.
bank.b0018: Not one job will go to people from here.
bank.b0019: The company's September 3 proposal lists many building jobs and fewer jobs after opening.
bank.b0020: The lights will go out in every house.
bank.b0021: Everyone's power bill will go down.
bank.b0022: The backup engines will run all day, every day.
bank.b0023: The company's September 3 proposal says the backup engines would run during power cuts and short tests.
bank.b0024: Every student will get a new laptop next month.
